corrections.measure: Personal allowance: increase by £235 to £9,440 in 2013-14, with equal gains to higher rate taxpayers
corrections.scope_note: Personal allowance increase with an offsetting basic-rate-limit cut so higher-rate taxpayers gain equally.
corrections.missing_machinery: No age/date-of-birth-related personal allowances or their separate income taper: personal_allowance computes one common amount and the GBP 100,000 ANI taper. Older taxpayers affected differently before 2016 cannot be represented by the common allowance reform.
corrections.expressibility_note: Raise personal_allowance.amount by £235 for 2013-14 and cut the basic rate limit (rates.uk[1].threshold, which is the band width after allowances) by £235 so the higher-rate threshold is unchanged; reversal construction. Both parameters start in 2015, so 2013-14 values must be added. Partial: separate age-related allowance machinery is absent (personal_allowance.py); this affects the tax change and downstream benefit response, beyond the separate dated-parameter gap.

corrections.measure: Personal allowance: increase by an additional £560 to £10,000 in 2014-15

corrections.missing_machinery: No age/date-of-birth-related personal allowances or their separate income taper: personal_allowance computes one common amount and the GBP 100,000 ANI taper. Older taxpayers affected differently before 2016 cannot be represented by the common allowance reform.
corrections.expressibility_note: Set personal_allowance.amount to £10,000 for 2014-15 and the basic rate limit (rates.uk[1].threshold) to keep the higher-rate threshold path; reversal construction. Both parameters start in 2015, so a 2014-15 value must be added. Partial: separate age-related allowance machinery is absent (personal_allowance.py); this affects the tax change and downstream benefit response, beyond the separate dated-parameter gap.

corrections.measure: Personal allowance: increase to £10,500 in 2015-16 with equal gains to higher rate taxpayers
corrections.scope_note: Personal allowance and basic rate limit are statutory income tax parameters on individuals.
corrections.missing_machinery: No age/date-of-birth-related personal allowances or their separate income taper: personal_allowance computes one common amount and the GBP 100,000 ANI taper. Older taxpayers affected differently before 2016 cannot be represented by the common allowance reform.
corrections.expressibility_note: Reform sets the PA to GBP 10,500 for 2015-16 and the basic rate limit so higher-rate payers gain the same cash as basic-rate payers, against a pre-Budget indexed baseline. The PA parameter starts 2015-04-06 at 10,600 (the later Autumn 2014 value), so both baseline and reform 2015-16 values have to be supplied. Partial: separate age-related allowance machinery is absent (personal_allowance.py); this affects the tax change and downstream benefit response, beyond the separate dated-parameter gap.

corrections.measure: Personal Allowance: increase to £10,600 in 2015-16 with full gains to higher rate taxpayers
corrections.scope_note: Personal allowance and basic rate limit are statutory income tax parameters on individuals.
corrections.missing_machinery: No age/date-of-birth-related personal allowances or their separate income taper: personal_allowance computes one common amount and the GBP 100,000 ANI taper. Older taxpayers affected differently before 2016 cannot be represented by the common allowance reform.
corrections.expressibility_note: Reform sets the PA to GBP 10,600 for 2015-16 with the higher-rate threshold rising by the full PA increase (basic rate limit held), against the Budget 2014 baseline (GBP 10,500). The PA parameter's first key (2015-04-06: 10,600) is this measure's value, so the baseline value has to be supplied. Partial: separate age-related allowance machinery is absent (personal_allowance.py); this affects the tax change and downstream benefit response, beyond the separate dated-parameter gap.

corrections.measure: Personal allowance: increase by £235 to £9,440 in 2013-14, with equal gains to higher rate taxpayers

corrections.missing_machinery: No age/date-of-birth-related personal allowances or their separate income taper: personal_allowance computes one common amount and the GBP 100,000 ANI taper. Older taxpayers affected differently before 2016 cannot be represented by the common allowance reform.

corrections.measure: Winter Fuel Payments: Target payments at recipients of Pension Credit and certain other means-tested benefits from winter 2024-25
corrections.scope_note: Winter Fuel Payment, a household cash entitlement, restricted to means-tested-benefit recipients.
corrections.missing_machinery: winter_fuel_allowance on_mtb omits Universal Credit and tax credits from the statutory qualifying benefits and cannot reproduce the full eligibility population; Scotland is excluded and England/Wales eligibility is not explicitly enforced for the benefit passport.
corrections.expressibility_note: Reversal: require_benefits false (installed true from 2024-01-01), read by winter_fuel_allowance. PE's qualifying-benefit test is pension_credit, income_support, esa_income and jsa_income (no UC or tax credits), Scotland is zeroed by the formula, and calendar 2024 proxies winter 2024-25; Pension Credit take-up responses in the costing are not modelled. Partial because UC/tax-credit passports in the 2024 regulations are absent, rather than solely a timing or behavioural discrepancy.

corrections.measure: Winter Fuel Payment: Target to pensioners with taxable income below or equal to £35,000 from Winter 2025
corrections.scope_note: Restores Winter Fuel Payment to pensioners with taxable income up to GBP 35,000.
corrections.missing_machinery: winter_fuel_allowance is a household eligibility payment using household.any of age and income; no individual Winter Fuel Payment allocation and tax recovery charge, so mixed-income pensioner couples cannot be represented faithfully. UC and tax-credit benefit passports are also absent; the threshold uses strict less-than.
corrections.expressibility_note: Reversal construction (registry): pre-measure world sets use_maximum_taxable_income false (means-tested-benefit passport only). The engine applies the GBP 35,000 test as eligibility (on total_income, England and Wales), whereas HMRC pays and claws back through income tax, so the PMD welfare and income-tax rows are netted in winter_fuel_allowance. Partial: the household income-passport shortcut omits individual split payments/recovery and the full benefit passport list.

corrections.measure: Capital Gains Tax: reduce the lifetime limit in entrepreneurs' relief to £1,000,000
corrections.scope_note: Capital gains tax relief on individuals' business disposals.
corrections.missing_machinery: No cumulative prior Business Asset Disposal/Entrepreneurs Relief usage input or formula: capital_gains_tax caps the current year relief gains at the lifetime limit as if none had been used before.
corrections.expressibility_note: The parameter already carries £10m to £1m on 2020-03-11 (FA 2020 Sch. 3); the reversal holds £10m. capital_gains_tax applies the limit to the year's capital_gains_badr as if none of it was used earlier, so lifetime-usage history is approximated. Forestalling and realisation responses in the costing are behavioural. Partial because changing a lifetime limit requires prior usage, not just the current annual relief-gains input.

corrections.measure: National Insurance: reverse temporary 1.25pp increase in NICs rates from November 2022, and cancel the Health and Social Care Levy
corrections.scope_note: Income tax knock-on of the NICs reversal and levy cancellation (employer NIC cut passed into pay); a household-tax consequence of an in-scope measure, mirroring autumn_budget_2021:tax:004.
corrections.missing_machinery: Only the employer-NIC pay pass-through channel exists (employer_ni_fixed_employer_cost_change, 100% immediate employee incidence by default, zero for earners below the secondary threshold); OBR's gradual incidence path, the deductibility of employer NICs for unincorporated employers (higher profits, more income tax) and the levy's over-SPA leg are not represented.
corrections.expressibility_note: Reversal construction as for tax:082/tax:084 (pre-measure world adds 1.25pp to the employer rate from 2022-11-06 and approximates the levy from 2023-24 as +1.25pp); in that scenario employer_ni_fixed_employer_cost_change lowers employment_income against the current-law baseline, so income_tax differs. Size rests on the incidence parameter, not OBR's assumption; annual processing samples the employer rate at the start of the period.

corrections.measure: Salary Sacrifice: Limit the value of salary sacrificed pension contributions that can receive employee and employer NICs relief to £2,000 per year from 6 April 2029
corrections.scope_note: Income tax head of the salary-sacrifice NICs cap: employers recouping the extra NICs through pay lowers taxable earnings; a household-tax consequence of an in-scope measure.
corrections.missing_machinery: PE's only channel is a uniform 0.16% employment-income haircut on all workers (PE's own calibration, not OBR's incidence); the PMD's 2029-30 +1,390 followed by -714 in 2030-31 implies further first-year or timing effects that PE has no machinery for.
corrections.expressibility_note: Reversal construction (cap inf in the pre-measure world, 2,000 from 2029-04-06 at 2.125.0): with the cap finite, salary_sacrifice_broad_base_haircut cuts employment_income by 0.16% for everyone, so income_tax falls; the redirected excess is relieved through pension_contributions_relief. Magnitude rests on the haircut parameter.

corrections.measure: National Insurance: maintain employer secondary threshold at current level from April 2023 until April 2028
corrections.scope_note: Income-tax head of an employer NIC threshold freeze; the engine contains an explicit employer-cost-to-pay channel.
corrections.missing_machinery: The employer-NI fixed-cost pay response is an immediate uniform incidence assumption (default 100%); the OBR gradual incidence path and unincorporated employers profits/deductibility channel are absent.
corrections.expressibility_note: Secondary threshold changes trigger employer_ni_fixed_employer_cost_change, included in employment_income. A reversal can change income_tax through pay, conditional on the incidence assumption; this does not reproduce every OBR cross-head channel.

corrections.measure: National Insurance contributions (NICs): 2p cut to the main rate of Class 1 employee NICs from January 2024
corrections.scope_note: Income-tax head of an employee NICs cut, with labour-supply and incorporation responses identified in the primary AS2023 policy costing.

PE can change earnings through its optional labour-supply response, which then changes income tax; the full OBR head cannot be represented. Harmonised with spring_budget_2024:tax:001.

corrections.scope_note: Income-tax head of a household CGT reform; scope describes the fiscal head, separately from whether its channel is available.

corrections.measure: Coronavirus job retention scheme
corrections.scope_note: Per-employee furlough wage support, or its direct payroll-tax head. Scope judgement includes employee-linked income support; the grant is paid to the employer and includes employer NIC/pension reimbursement.
corrections.missing_machinery: No CJRS grant formula, furlough status/hours, reference-pay input, phase-specific government contribution rule or no-support employment counterfactual. Payroll taxes exist but the scheme-driven earnings base does not.
corrections.expressibility_note: Treasury Direction 15 April 2020 paras 2.2 and 8.1 links reimbursement to specified employees pay and employer NIC/pension costs. Classify as household-relevant wage support, with the employer composite noted; existing annual employment-income inputs alone cannot construct the scheme.

corrections.measure: Reduce social sector rents by 1% each year for 4 years from 2016-17
corrections.scope_note: Lower rents paid by social-tenant households, or the resulting household housing-benefit saving. The receipts head also includes the public landlords side.
corrections.missing_machinery: Only a UK-wide social-rent projection index exists, applied to non-private-rented households before data load; no English social-landlord rent-setting rule. uprate_rent hard-skips years before 2022, so a 2016 replay additionally needs a formula guard change and historical indices. Public landlords receipts are not a PE government fiscal variable.
corrections.expressibility_note: Todays uprate_rent reads social_rent growth for non-private tenures. This provides a partial future-year level proxy; it cannot perform the 2016-19 reform dates as shipped because of the pre-2022 guard, nor target English providers. Historical readiness remains blocked.
